page: Amazon Web Services r6gd.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by the 64-bit ARM architecture. Built on AWS Graviton processors with Neoverse-N1 cores clocked at 2.5 GHz, the instance supplies 16 physical cores across 16 dedicated vCPUs with single-threaded execution per core. Operating on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor, it provides 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a dedicated 950 GB NVMe SSD instance storage volume and a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight solid multi-threaded throughput balanced against modest per-core performance. The instance achieved 24,282.92 on multi-core stress-ng tests and 8,586.0 on multi-core Geekbench, reflecting typical mid-tier throughput for 16-core ARM deployments. Conversely, single-thread evaluations registered in the lower quartiles, including a single-core Geekbench rating of 975.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 20.3 GB/sec. Memory subsystem bandwidth maintains steady mid-range throughput, sustaining 162.96 GB/sec in 256 MB uncached reads and 74.01 GB/sec during uncached writes.

The inclusion of a 950 GB direct-attached NVMe solid-state drive delivers low-latency scratch space without relying solely on network-attached storage. The hardware design proves cost-efficient for scale-out memory workloads due to Graviton's power profile and the 1:8 core-to-memory configuration. Primary trade-offs include subdued performance on serial execution paths, reduced cryptographic testing output (2,168.13 in PassMark encryption), and low throughput in text-generation tasks, where small-model inference drops into the lower percentiles.

Given its high RAM density, dedicated local NVMe disk, and mid-range concurrency, the r6gd.4xlarge is well tailored for in-memory caching solutions like Redis, intermediate data-processing jobs, relational or document database instances, and distributed analytics pipelines that demand substantial memory footprints and fast local transient storage.
description: Amazon Web Services r6gd.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 16 dedicated physical cores powered by the 64-bit ARM Neoverse-N1 architecture at 2.5 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, it achieves an 8.0 GB per core ratio and includes a bundled 950 GB NVMe SSD instance store alongside 5 Gbps baseline network capacity. Multi-core performance is solid, posting 24,282.92 in stress-ng and supporting 20.4 million Redis SET operations per second, though single-threaded computational tasks and LLM inference rank lower across synthetic benchmarks. The inclusion of low-latency direct-attached NVMe storage alongside substantial memory density creates an efficient profile for memory-heavy transactional systems, in-memory caches, distributed processing engines, and database servers needing high local I/O.
